_about: Comparison and proposal summary. The build shows these on the landing page and writes COMPARISON.md and PROPOSAL.md from them, so the three always agree.
title: APARN website redesign: three prototypes
intro: Three directions for a new website for the Asia Pacific Artistic Research Network (APARN), prepared for Dr Roopesh Sitharan, Director of APARN. All three use the same checked content and the same functions, so they can be compared fairly. They differ in look, tone and the way you move through them.
note: These are proposal demos, not the official APARN website. aparn.net is unchanged. Search engines are asked not to index these pages.

concepts.name: Concept A: Editorial Gallery
concepts.line: Calm, cultured and inviting, like a contemporary arts publication or a carefully made exhibition catalogue.
concepts.direction: Warm ivory pages, dark ink and one cinnabar accent. Newsreader, a reading serif, carries the headings and text, with Work Sans for small labels. Generous margins, clear section headings and artworks given room to breathe. Original “isles” plates, a horizon of island shapes, mark each conference year.
concepts.ux: A guided journey down the home page: discover APARN, see its activity, meet the network, find a way to take part. The network explorer is a tabbed index of people, places, activities and practices beside a reading panel; choosing an item rewrites the panel and marks what it connects to. Stories open in place and the archive is a horizontal timeline.
strengths: Reads easily and feels trustworthy to researchers, institutions and partners.
Gives artworks, writing and research the most room.
A quiet structure that will age well and is simple to maintain.
Very clear on phones: one column, large type and a simple menu.
tradeoffs: Less immediate energy: activity is described more than shown.
Depends on strong images and good writing to stay lively.
Exploring the network is calmer and asks for a little more reading.

concepts.name: Concept B: Living Network
concepts.line: An active artistic network and a digital exhibition: explore first, then join, share and publish.
concepts.direction: White and black with flat blocks of jade, lacquer red and turmeric. Archivo throughout: condensed at poster scale for headings, normal width for reading. An asymmetric but ordered composition with exhibition strips, and an original poster card for every gathering, each with its own colour and shape.
concepts.ux: Exploration comes first. The connection board sets people, places, activities, and practices and outputs side by side: pick any one and everything it connects to lights up, with lines on wide screens and its story beside it. Clear next steps follow: join, share your work, publish. A black bar keeps Explore, Take part, Publish and Join APARN in reach, with a full-screen index.
strengths: Shows the network’s reach and activity at a glance.
Memorable and distinctive among artistic research websites.
Turns the network data into something to explore, and every connection shown is sourced.
Strong, repeated invitations to join and take part.
tradeoffs: Louder: the heavy type needs restraint on long text pages.
The board is dense on small phones, where it becomes stacked lists with the story first.
More design rules to follow when adding content, such as poster colours and shapes.

concepts.name: Concept C: Clear Signal
concepts.line: White, precise and technological: the clearest hierarchy of the three, with smooth motion that guides the eye.
concepts.direction: White pages, near-black text and one deep blue accent close to International Klein Blue, a nod to both art history and the screen. Roboto in a strict type scale: one clear title per section, a short lead, no small labels above titles. Rounded buttons and cards, thin lines, and an original two-line transit diagram of every gathering since 2019.
concepts.ux: A tidy home page with a section index and a back-to-top button; every link within a page scrolls smoothly up or down. Content glides in from the direction you scroll, figures count up, buttons respond to a press and pages fade into each other. The network explorer is an orbit: choose anything and its connections arrange around it, so you can hop from person to place to event.
strengths: The clearest hierarchy and the quickest to scan.
Feels current and technological while staying calm.
Motion explains relationships (the orbit, the transit lines) rather than decorating.
Familiar and comfortable on phones: rounded buttons, a full-screen menu, smooth scrolling.
tradeoffs: Less artistic character than A or B; the artworks and diagrams carry the personality.
The most motion of the three, so it needs care to stay calm and fast. It switches off for visitors who ask for reduced motion.
White, rounded interfaces are common; the blue accent and the diagrams keep it distinct.

shared: “Join APARN” opens the APARN Google Group. It sits in the header, the phone menu, the opening screen, after the network section and in a closing invitation, with a note that joining happens on Google Groups.
Across the network: dated evidence that keeps members, conference participation, host locations and project locations apart.

Three ways to take part, each with a status label: the APARN Conference (next: APARN2027 at RMIT University Vietnam, details to be confirmed), the APARN Gathering at the SAR Conference (proposed 5–10-minute updates; SAR 2027 runs 21–23 April 2027 in Bratislava) and the APARN Annual Publication (proposed).
One template, one contribution, two uses, with the “Template for Annual Publication” button on the home page, the publication page, the SAR gathering page and the start of the submission journey.
The template as an editable DOCX, a PDF reading copy and a web preview, with a presentation guide built on the same structure.
A submission demo in four steps: download, prepare, add details, review. It asks only for what is needed, the publication checkbox starts unchecked, and nothing is uploaded, sent or stored.
An archive of every gathering since 2019, with programmes, organisers and links to the published work.
Content kept in JSON files, pages readable without JavaScript, keyboard and screen-reader support, reduced motion respected, and layouts checked at 360, 768 and 1440 pixels.

proposal.to: Dr Roopesh Sitharan, Director of APARN
proposal.summary: The current aparn.net is accurate but static and text-heavy. All three prototypes keep every verified fact and add what the site is missing: a clear way in, visible activity across the region, simple navigation, artistic character and one easy path from a short SAR update to the year-end publication.

points.title: Joining is always one step away
points.text: “Join APARN” is the strongest button on every page and goes straight to the Google Group. A line beside it says that joining happens on Google Groups, and five benefits explain why to join, each backed by a dated source.

points.title: International activity you can see
points.text: Across the network brings together people, places, events and published work: 11 documented places plus the online editions, eight annual meetings since 2019 and 28 pieces in APARN’s JAR channel. Figures are dated and never mix conference participation with membership. Member locations stay private until APARN approves data to show.

points.title: Navigation that stays simple
points.text: Concepts A and C use five sections and Concept B three, in place of a long list of event pages. Every past event has its own archive page, and every address works as a direct link.

points.title: Artistic character
points.text: Credited artworks from APARN’s own events, original graphics for each concept and warm, direct wording. The three directions offer a calm editorial voice, an energetic exhibition voice or a clear, technological one.

points.title: From SAR update to publication
points.text: One template, one contribution, two uses: prepare one contribution, share a 5–10-minute update at the APARN Gathering at the SAR Conference, and opt in to the year-end collection. The demo shows the whole journey honestly, and the README sets out what a live submission service would need.

proposal.ask: Please choose a direction (or a mix), confirm the open items below, and approve the draft template limits. With those answers the chosen concept can be prepared for launch.
